translations.answer: FB-CPR can infer reward, goal, and tracking tasks without policy retraining in a simulated SMPL humanoid, but robot use still requires morphology retargeting, dynamics tracking, constraint enforcement, and independent hardware validation.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Tasks can be expressed by rewards, goals, or reference states represented in the learned occupancy space.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Robot transfer adds morphology adaptation and a dynamics-feasible low-level controller.
translations.applicability.environments.0: HumEnv reward, goal, and tracking tasks.
translations.applicability.robots.0: The paper evaluates only a simulated SMPL humanoid.
translations.confidence_rationale: A broad benchmark and official implementation support unified zero-shot task inference in simulation; no robot hardware evidence supports direct WBC deployment.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines FB-CPR and evaluates reward, goal, and tracking inference with ablations and human preference.
translations.evidence.0.title: Zero-Shot Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Behavioral Foundation Models
translations.title: Can zero-shot behavioral foundation-model control directly serve as a humanoid robot WBC?
